newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Tuesday said four percent of the U.S. winter wheat crop was in very poor condition, 12 percent poor, 33 percent fair, 43 percent good and eight percent excellent.
In its report on conditions for the week ended May 25, USDA said 95 percent of the U.S. corn crop was planted versus 76 percent a year ago and the five-year average of 81 percent.
It said 70 percent of the U.S. soybean crop was planted compared with 32 percent a year ago and the five-year average of 45 percent.
USDA said three percent of the U.S. spring wheat crop was in very poor condition, three percent poor, 25 percent fair, 62 percent good and seven percent excellent.

The department reported 77 percent of the cotton crop was planted, compared with 75 percent in the same period in 1996 and the five-year average of 77 percent. -- Washington Commodities Desk (202) 898-8394
